# lance-file: file versions and entry points

**INCOMPLETE.** Fifty-four of 56 inventory entries are analyzed (25,581 physical text/symlink lines plus 1,139,328 binary bytes). Schema conversion, encoding IO adapter, exact dispatch, current-version composition/compression selection, shared structural projection, writer facade and type checks are covered. Exact current reader metadata/projection modules and V2_1/V2_2/V2_3 writer wrappers/shared pipeline are covered; V2_0 writer, testing utilities and compatibility test/generator sources are covered in the [V2_0/compatibility supplement](rust-lance-file-v20-compatibility.md). The complete [writer-test catalog](rust-lance-file-writer-tests.md) is also covered. The [shared reader](rust-lance-file-shared-reader.md) now covers full/indexed metadata loading, local caching, read dispatch and tests. The [concat supplement](rust-lance-file-concat.md) covers complete-file assembly and Blob part validation. The [V1 foundation supplement](rust-lance-file-v1-foundation.md) covers projection, dictionary dispatch, metadata and page tables; the [V1 concrete codec supplement](rust-lance-file-v1-codecs.md) covers binary/plain/dictionary implementations. The [full V1 reader](rust-lance-file-v1-reader.md) and [V1 writer](rust-lance-file-v1-writer.md), including its [full statistics implementation](rust-lance-file-v1-statistics.md), are covered; the [complete benchmark catalog](rust-lance-file-benchmarks.md) is covered; the complete [V1 fixture byte map](rust-lance-file-binary-fixtures.md) and both [embedded V2_0 fixtures](rust-lance-file-embedded-fixtures.md) are covered. Modern encoding/IO scheduler implementations and two standard V2_1/V2_2 binary fixture payloads remain pending. README describes an internal crate not intended for external use, despite public Rust modules. (rust/lance-file/README.md:1-6)

[Orientation](../L0-orientation.md) · [Table metadata](rust-lance-table.md) · [Format](../L3-symbols/format-spec.md) · [Scenarios](../L4-crosscutting/scenarios.md) · [Build/test](../L4-crosscutting/build-and-test.md)

## Responsibility and routes

The crate declares readers/writers for the Lance file format. Its facade exports concat,datatypes,format,reader,testing,version,versions,writer; io is crate-visible with LanceEncodingsIo publicly reexported; compatibility_tests is private under cfg(test). The [runtime-boundary supplement](rust-lance-file-runtime.md) covers schema conversion, IO adaptation, exact dispatch and writer interfaces; the [structural writer supplement](rust-lance-file-structural-writer.md) covers current structural writer lifecycles, and the [V2_0/compatibility supplement](rust-lance-file-v20-compatibility.md) covers the separate array writer and fixture harness. Shared reader loading/cache/projection orchestration is covered in the [shared reader supplement](rust-lance-file-shared-reader.md); V1 foundations and concrete binary/plain/dictionary codecs are covered separately; the [full V1 reader](rust-lance-file-v1-reader.md) is covered. Delegated modern encoding/IO scheduling remain pending. (rust/lance-file/README.md:3-6; rust/lance-file/src/lib.rs:4-17)

```text
lance_file
|-- version: request policy -> exact identity -> metadata/footer codecs
|-- determine_file_version: size -> last8 bytes -> magic -> exact identity
|-- format: generated pb / pbfile, LANC magic and legacy0.2 constants
|-- io: range splitting, empty placeholders and ordered reassembly
|-- datatypes: flat protobuf fields <-> core schema trees
|-- versions: exact dispatch, composition/policies, current reader grammar and all exact V2 writers
|   `-- v1: projection/dictionary dispatch/metadata/page table, concrete codecs, reader/writer and statistics covered
|-- writer: facade/options/type checks and shared structural pipeline covered
|-- reader: full/indexed metadata, cache, projections, read dispatch and tests covered
|-- concat: compatibility, Blob part gates, page relocation and output lifecycle
|-- testing: public local-file/cache helpers, collecting IO
`-- compatibility_tests: private cfg(test), pinned stable bytes / current unstable determinism
```

Routes follow rust/lance-file/src/lib.rs:4-60 and rust/lance-file/src/version.rs:19-262. No capability is inferred from numeric release order.

See [current composition and structural projection](rust-lance-file-composition.md) for ordered version policies and shared metadata contracts.

See [exact reader grammar](rust-lance-file-readers.md) for metadata validation order and version-specific acceptance.

## Caller requests and persisted identities

LanceFileVersion is a caller selector with Legacy,V2_0,V2_1,Stable,V2_2,Next,V2_3. Default is exact V2_2. resolve() maps Stable->V2_2,Next->V2_3 and exact variants to themselves (Legacy->V1). is_unstable is true only after resolving to V2_3. Display/serde preserve stable/next as strings; they are request serialization, not strict persisted identity codecs. (rust/lance-file/src/version.rs:19-127)

FromStr lowercases but does not trim. Accepted aliases are0.1/legacy,2.0/0.3,2.1,2.2,2.3,stable,next. ConcreteFileVersion has only V1,V2_0,V2_1,V2_2,V2_3, derives Hash but no ordering, and has no Default/serde/FromStr implementation here. Strict from_manifest_string accepts canonical0.1/2.0/2.1/2.2/2.3 only. to_selector always produces exact variants, losing prior policy intent. (rust/lance-file/src/version.rs:92-107; rust/lance-file/src/version.rs:128-197)

| Exact identity | Manifest string | DataFile metadata(u32,u32) | Standard footer(u16,u16) | Embedded footer(u16,u16) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| V1 |0.1 |(0,2) |(0,2) |(0,2) |
| V2_0 |2.0 |(2,0) |(0,3) |(2,0) |
| V2_1 |2.1 |(2,1) |(2,1) |(2,1) |
| V2_2 |2.2 |(2,2) |(2,2) |(2,2) |
| V2_3 |2.3 |(2,3) |(2,3) |(2,3) |

Both numeric decoders accept(0,0..=2) as V1 and(0,3)/(2,0) as V2_0, plus the other listed exact pairs. They reject everything else with InvalidInput Unknown Lance storage version: value. Strict string decoding rejects0.3 even though request parsing and numeric footer alias handling accept their respective historical forms. The table describes mapping functions, not proof every writer calls them. (rust/lance-file/src/version.rs:172-272)

## Footer detection and errors

determine_file_version takes ObjectStore,Path,optional known usize size. If unknown, await store.size and checked-convert; if known, trust it. Reject size<8, await open_with_size and get_range(size-8..size), require footer[4..]==LANC, decode first four bytes as LEu16 major/minor and dispatch exact parser. IO errors propagate; size/magic/version errors are InvalidInput. Fewer than4 returned bytes could panic because no explicit received-length check precedes slicing. (rust/lance-file/src/lib.rs:25-60; rust/lance-file/src/format.rs:30-33)

This reads only the final8 bytes and does not verify pages, schema, full footer structure or data validity. The local async fixture uses synthetic8-byte legacy footers with no data. Known size avoids the explicit size call, but underlying store.open behavior and total request count remain pending. (rust/lance-file/src/lib.rs:30-59; rust/lance-file/src/version.rs:411-430)

## Dependencies, features and build

Package metadata/toolchain/lints inherit workspace. Runtime dependencies declare Lance Arrow/core/encoding/IO, Arrow arithmetic/array/buffer/cast/data/schema/select, async-recursion/async-trait, byteorder/bytes, datafusion-common, futures/log/num-traits, object_store,prost/prost-types,serde,tokio,tracing. Exact dependency versions, transitive features and exhaustive use-site reasons remain pending root/dependency analysis; reviewed code uses core errors/deepsize, serde and store/path types. (rust/lance-file/Cargo.toml:1-40; rust/lance-file/src/version.rs:4-11; rust/lance-file/src/lib.rs:19-23)

Dev dependencies are lance-datagen,lance-testing,criterion,rstest,proptest,pretty_assertions,rand,test-log,libc. Build dependencies prost-build and optional protobuf-src support protoc feature. docs.rs requests that feature; its Ubuntu rationale is a source comment, not a live service check. Reader/schema benches disable the standard harness. (rust/lance-file/Cargo.toml:41-72)

build.rs optionally sets PROTOC through unsafe process-environment mutation, enables proto3 optional, maps .lance.encodings to lance_encoding::format::pb and compiles shared file/file2/encodings_v2_0/encodings_v2_1 schemas. ## Extension boundary

Keep caller selectors distinct from exact storage identities; a new exact version needs explicit string/data-metadata/standard-footer/embedded-footer mapping and explicit capabilities elsewhere. Do not infer support by ordering, persist Stable/Next in manifests, or collapse the v2.0 footer alias distinction. The local tests pin these mappings but do not establish full historical reader/writer compatibility. Exact reader/writer dispatch and shared type checks are now covered in the runtime-boundary supplement; all exact V2 writer mechanisms and compatibility test/generator sources are now covered. Shared reader orchestration and tests are covered; encoding byte algorithms, delegated IO/decoder scheduling, remaining V2 binary fixture payloads remain pending. (rust/lance-file/src/version.rs:29-50; rust/lance-file/src/version.rs:128-262; rust/lance-file/src/version.rs:291-430)

## Projection and field mapping

Visit fields in preorder, emitting the parent and then children. Blob and packed-struct fields each occupy one slot and stop recursion, while ordinary struct/container parents also occupy slots even when they have no data page. data_file_columns returns original signed IDs paired with consecutive signed physical indices from0. It does not validate empty/repeated/out-of-bounds indices or remove unmatched schema fields. Column-name projection builds the full original mapping before delegating Schema::project, then selects original physical indices. ## Dictionary dispatch and mutation order

read_binary_array accepts exactly Utf8,Binary,LargeUtf8,LargeBinary, converts parameters first and dispatches to the corresponding BinaryDecoder; other types return InvalidInput. read_fixed_stride_array checks the local fixed-stride predicate, returns Schema on false, constructs PlainDecoder, then converts parameters and awaits get. Neither wrapper independently checks offsets or response sizes. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:35-90)

write_schema_dictionaries scans every ID from0 through max_field_id, skipping holes/nondictionaries. Missing dictionary metadata is IO; missing values is InvalidInput. The actual array type chooses numeric PlainEncoder or binary-like BinaryEncoder; unsupported values give Schema. Only successful encode updates offset/length. Earlier writes and mutations survive later errors; no transaction, shutdown or abort is provided. Cost includes sparse ID-span traversal and repeated schema lookup. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:92-132)

Hydration recursively processes nondictionary roots/children in order. For a dictionary it uses the schema value type, reads the entire stored region and replaces values, even when values was already Some. Binary values use nullable=true; only eight signed/unsigned integer types take the fixed-stride branch. It does not recurse below a dictionary node. async_recursion boxes recursion without explicit task spawning; successful earlier fields remain mutated on error/cancellation. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:134-192)

Write and read predicates are asymmetric. The write side asks is_numeric rather than the read side's explicit integer whitelist. The local is_binary_like also accepts Utf8View/BinaryView, which the four-type binary reader rejects. Concrete BinaryEncoder also rejects both view types; PlainEncoder writes fixed-width numeric buffers, while hydration retains its narrower integer whitelist. Metadata stores Vec<i32> cumulative batch offsets, usize page-table position, Option manifest position and optional statistics. # V2_0 writer and exact-version compatibility harness

**PARTIAL CRATE COVERAGE.** This supplement covers 1,997 lines across the concrete V2_0 writer, testing helpers, compatibility tests and three fixture-provenance/generator files. The [shared reader](rust-lance-file-shared-reader.md) covers current reader IO/cache orchestration. Binary fixture payloads, delegated scheduling, legacy writer/reader internals and encoding byte algorithms remain pending. Tests and generators were read, not run.

[Crate](rust-lance-file.md) · [Structural writers](rust-lance-file-structural-writer.md) · [Reader grammar](rust-lance-file-readers.md) · [Orientation](../L0-orientation.md) · [Contracts](../L3-symbols/behavior-contracts.md) · [Format](../L3-symbols/format-spec.md) · [Scenarios](../L4-crosscutting/scenarios.md) · [Build and tests](../L4-crosscutting/build-and-test.md)

## Concrete V2_0 ownership and initialization

Writer owns its own object writer, optional schema/type cache, field encoders, physical column metadata/mapping, per-field and aggregate row counts, global descriptors, schema metadata, boxed ArrayFieldEncodingStrategy, options and spill state. It does not compose the shared structural pipeline. Public Writer is reexported from its exact-version parent; the footer helper is effectively internal and reached through parent embedded-batch functions. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:153-218; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/mod.rs:21-32; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:852-856)

```text
V2_0 Writer
|-- ArrayFieldEncodingStrategy -> BatchEncoder -> FieldEncoder list
|-- schema + expected types + schema metadata
|-- physical column metadata + field mapping
|-- per-field counts -> aggregate maximum/logical length
|-- ObjectWriter + user global-buffer descriptors
'-- optional spill: Pending(store,path) -> Active(sidecar,chunk index)
```

Eager construction creates lazy state then initializes. Lazy construction stores inputs and allocates the default strategy without validation or IO. Initialization validates explicit options, computes cache/page limits, validates schema and constructs BatchEncoder before installing encoders/metadata/mapping. It divides a supplied total cache budget by top-level field count; with an empty schema this can divide by zero before schema validation. Defaults are 8 MiB per root field, 32 MiB max page, keep_original_array=false and alignment64. An explicit max-page value wins over the environment; malformed environment text warns and defaults, missing/non-Unicode text silently defaults, and an environment value of zero bypasses the explicit Some(0) rejection. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:184-218; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:326-369; rust/lance-file/src/writer.rs:56-65)

## Preparation and row mutation

write_batch initializes from its first Arrow schema, checks ExpectedTypes, selects every required field by name and prepares every field array before testing for an empty batch or the single-batch u32 limit. Missing fields fail even for empty batches. FieldEncoder::prepare_array defaults to identity and documents preparation before state mutation; concrete validation/transformation remains encoder-defined. No separate recursive nullability walk appears in this writer. The structural pipeline instead performs its own logical-nullability validation. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:313-324; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:371-400; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:451-476; rust/lance-encoding/src/encoder.rs:175-183; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:598-627)

Encoding snapshots each field's old row number, calls maybe_encode, writes out-of-line buffers, then checks aggregate u64 overflow. Counters advance before ordered page tasks and flush finish, so later failure does not rewind them. Batch counters use original batch.num_rows while encoding uses prepared array lengths; the caller/encoder relationship must preserve these lengths. write_column checks schema/index/input size/type, prepares one array, returns if that prepared array is empty, then advances only that field by its prepared length with unchecked addition and updates the aggregate maximum. A previously initialized lazy writer satisfies its schema check despite the explicit-schema wording in the error. Unequal root-field lengths are allowed. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:402-506; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:507-584)

FuturesOrdered emits task results in insertion order; pages are written sequentially, followed by writer flush. The first error stops the loop and drops remaining local futures. The code comment describes flush as observing failed uploads without waiting for all in-flight uploads; backend implementation, spawned-work cancellation and durability are still outside this scope. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:279-300)

## Buffer placement, spill and completion

Ordinary page, batch-external, global and column buffers get trailing 0x48 padding based on their payload length to64. Their starts are not repaired. V2_0 write_external_buffer writes completely raw at current position, unlike the structural sink's leading-zero alignment. Page metadata records raw lengths and wraps either page-description family in Any/Direct without checking the exact V2_0 grammar. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:41-41; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:231-262; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:703-708; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:831-849; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:352-360)

Spill threshold per column is max(256 KiB/max(column_count,1),64). One message can overshoot; buffers retain capacity and chunk descriptors grow. Pending is removed before awaited sidecar creation, after page payload IO. A failed creation loses pending state. Finish removes metadata/spill state, shuts down and reopens the sidecar, reconstructs all pages for each column and replaces that column's prior page vector. Late spill can therefore discard descriptions retained before activation. Cleanup is explicitly caller-owned and no local deletion occurs. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:48-146; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:219-228; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:263-275; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:597-630)

finish flushes encoders, consumes/finishes them if present, writes descriptor and user-global table entries, column metadata, column offset table, global offset table, footer, then awaits shutdown. Descriptor and column metadata are raw protobuf bytes; each offset-table entry is a 16-byte LE(position,length) pair. Schema metadata is drained and blobs unloaded before descriptor IO. External-metadata initialization bypasses validation and replaces schema/metadata/aggregate rows without rebuilding encoder, type-cache, mapping or field-count state. It can support footer-only external output, but subsequent ordinary writes require coherent state the initializer does not establish. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:586-709; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:768-829)

Two position assumptions need preservation: finish_writers writes out-of-line buffers raw while the planner advances virtual positions by payload plus padding; column-buffer offsets advance by payload length while actual writes include padding. Multiple unaligned buffers can violate those assumptions. These are source deductions, not evidence that current encoder producers emit such shapes. The final physical-column count mismatch panics unconditionally. No finished flag or rollback protects repeat calls; abort is an empty async body and does not drop the writer. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:711-759; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:831-834; rust/lance-encoding/src/encoder.rs:130-159)

| Footer-relative bytes | Standard V2_0 | Embedded V2_0 |
|---|---|---|
| 0–7 | column metadata start, LEu64 | same meaning |
| 8–15 | column offset table start, LEu64 | same meaning |

# V2_0 writer and exact-version compatibility harness

**PARTIAL CRATE COVERAGE.** This supplement covers 1,997 lines across the concrete V2_0 writer, testing helpers, compatibility tests and three fixture-provenance/generator files. The [shared reader](rust-lance-file-shared-reader.md) covers current reader IO/cache orchestration. Binary fixture payloads, delegated scheduling, legacy writer/reader internals and encoding byte algorithms remain pending. Tests and generators were read, not run.

[Crate](rust-lance-file.md) · [Structural writers](rust-lance-file-structural-writer.md) · [Reader grammar](rust-lance-file-readers.md) · [Orientation](../L0-orientation.md) · [Contracts](../L3-symbols/behavior-contracts.md) · [Format](../L3-symbols/format-spec.md) · [Scenarios](../L4-crosscutting/scenarios.md) · [Build and tests](../L4-crosscutting/build-and-test.md)

## Concrete V2_0 ownership and initialization

Writer owns its own object writer, optional schema/type cache, field encoders, physical column metadata/mapping, per-field and aggregate row counts, global descriptors, schema metadata, boxed ArrayFieldEncodingStrategy, options and spill state. It does not compose the shared structural pipeline. Public Writer is reexported from its exact-version parent; the footer helper is effectively internal and reached through parent embedded-batch functions. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:153-218; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/mod.rs:21-32; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:852-856)

```text
V2_0 Writer
|-- ArrayFieldEncodingStrategy -> BatchEncoder -> FieldEncoder list
|-- schema + expected types + schema metadata
|-- physical column metadata + field mapping
|-- per-field counts -> aggregate maximum/logical length
|-- ObjectWriter + user global-buffer descriptors
'-- optional spill: Pending(store,path) -> Active(sidecar,chunk index)
```

Eager construction creates lazy state then initializes. Lazy construction stores inputs and allocates the default strategy without validation or IO. Initialization validates explicit options, computes cache/page limits, validates schema and constructs BatchEncoder before installing encoders/metadata/mapping. It divides a supplied total cache budget by top-level field count; with an empty schema this can divide by zero before schema validation. Defaults are 8 MiB per root field, 32 MiB max page, keep_original_array=false and alignment64. An explicit max-page value wins over the environment; malformed environment text warns and defaults, missing/non-Unicode text silently defaults, and an environment value of zero bypasses the explicit Some(0) rejection. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:184-218; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:326-369; rust/lance-file/src/writer.rs:56-65)

## Preparation and row mutation

write_batch initializes from its first Arrow schema, checks ExpectedTypes, selects every required field by name and prepares every field array before testing for an empty batch or the single-batch u32 limit. Missing fields fail even for empty batches. FieldEncoder::prepare_array defaults to identity and documents preparation before state mutation; concrete validation/transformation remains encoder-defined. No separate recursive nullability walk appears in this writer. The structural pipeline instead performs its own logical-nullability validation. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:313-324; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:371-400; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:451-476; rust/lance-encoding/src/encoder.rs:175-183; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:598-627)

Encoding snapshots each field's old row number, calls maybe_encode, writes out-of-line buffers, then checks aggregate u64 overflow. Counters advance before ordered page tasks and flush finish, so later failure does not rewind them. Batch counters use original batch.num_rows while encoding uses prepared array lengths; the caller/encoder relationship must preserve these lengths. write_column checks schema/index/input size/type, prepares one array, returns if that prepared array is empty, then advances only that field by its prepared length with unchecked addition and updates the aggregate maximum. A previously initialized lazy writer satisfies its schema check despite the explicit-schema wording in the error. Unequal root-field lengths are allowed. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:402-506; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:507-584)

FuturesOrdered emits task results in insertion order; pages are written sequentially, followed by writer flush. The first error stops the loop and drops remaining local futures. The code comment describes flush as observing failed uploads without waiting for all in-flight uploads; backend implementation, spawned-work cancellation and durability are still outside this scope. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:279-300)

## Buffer placement, spill and completion

Ordinary page, batch-external, global and column buffers get trailing 0x48 padding based on their payload length to64. Their starts are not repaired. V2_0 write_external_buffer writes completely raw at current position, unlike the structural sink's leading-zero alignment. Page metadata records raw lengths and wraps either page-description family in Any/Direct without checking the exact V2_0 grammar. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:41-41; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:231-262; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:703-708; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:831-849; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:352-360)

Spill threshold per column is max(256 KiB/max(column_count,1),64). One message can overshoot; buffers retain capacity and chunk descriptors grow. Pending is removed before awaited sidecar creation, after page payload IO. A failed creation loses pending state. Finish removes metadata/spill state, shuts down and reopens the sidecar, reconstructs all pages for each column and replaces that column's prior page vector. Late spill can therefore discard descriptions retained before activation. Cleanup is explicitly caller-owned and no local deletion occurs. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:48-146; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:219-228; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:263-275; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:597-630)

finish flushes encoders, consumes/finishes them if present, writes descriptor and user-global table entries, column metadata, column offset table, global offset table, footer, then awaits shutdown. Descriptor and column metadata are raw protobuf bytes; each offset-table entry is a 16-byte LE(position,length) pair. Schema metadata is drained and blobs unloaded before descriptor IO. External-metadata initialization bypasses validation and replaces schema/metadata/aggregate rows without rebuilding encoder, type-cache, mapping or field-count state. It can support footer-only external output, but subsequent ordinary writes require coherent state the initializer does not establish. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:586-709; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:768-829)

Two position assumptions need preservation: finish_writers writes out-of-line buffers raw while the planner advances virtual positions by payload plus padding; column-buffer offsets advance by payload length while actual writes include padding. Multiple unaligned buffers can violate those assumptions. These are source deductions, not evidence that current encoder producers emit such shapes. The final physical-column count mismatch panics unconditionally. No finished flag or rollback protects repeat calls; abort is an empty async body and does not drop the writer. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:711-759; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:831-834; rust/lance-encoding/src/encoder.rs:130-159)

## Exact footer identity

| Footer-relative bytes | Standard V2_0 | Embedded V2_0 |
|---|---|---|
| 0–7 | column metadata start, LEu64 | same meaning |
| 8–15 | column offset table start, LEu64 | same meaning |
| 16–23 | global offset table start, LEu64 | same meaning |
| 24–27 | global-buffer count, LEu32 | zero in mini; one in self-described |
| 28–31 | physical-column count, LEu32 | page_table length |
| 32–33 | major0, LEu16 | major2, LEu16 |
| 34–35 | minor3, LEu16 | minor0, LEu16 |
| 36–39 | LANC | LANC |

These literal branches are independent implementations. The version decoder accepts both as V2_0, and tests distinguish standard and embedded mappings. concat_lance_footer copies input bytes and given page/column descriptors, optionally appends a cloned core schema without blob unloading, then metadata/tables/footer. It ignores ColumnInfo.index and top_level_columns and does not validate supplied buffer positions or grammar. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:812-828; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:852-952; rust/lance-file/src/version.rs:226-262; rust/lance-file/src/compatibility_tests.rs:379-448)

The deterministic input has 4,097 rows and five fields: Int32 IDs, nullable UTF8 names (every7th null), nullable Int32 lists (every11th null, every5th second child null), nullable Int8/UTF8 dictionary keys (every13th null), and nonnull LargeBinary payloads in a nullable blob-marked field. Compression metadata disables name and dictionary-value compression. Standard writers receive five batches of up to1,024 rows; embedded V2_0 uses only id/name for the first257 rows. (rust/lance-file/src/compatibility_tests.rs:36-98; rust/lance-file/src/compatibility_tests.rs:232-315; rust/lance-file/src/compatibility_tests.rs:401-408)

Stable cases compare complete current bytes to baseline includes, assert exact footer identity and read the baseline through the current reader. Read assertions include at least one multi-page physical column, full row count/schema equality and ordered value/null equality. Blob comparison ignores physical bytes under nulls. V2_3 instead writes twice in the same revision and checks equal bytes plus roundtrip; it has no checked historical fixture. The V1 test explicitly expects null lists as empty, null child integers as zero and null dictionary keys as green. The full V1 reader and writer are now independently traced in their supplements; this test still establishes only the stated fixture oracle. (rust/lance-file/src/compatibility_tests.rs:100-230; rust/lance-file/src/compatibility_tests.rs:318-524)

FsFixture exposes a local store, temp path and testing scheduler. write_lance_file collects the entire input, adds foo=bar to writer schema, finishes and returns original schema/data/mapping. read_lance_file requires that metadata, reads RangeFull with batch1024/readahead16 and collects all output. count_lance_file fully decodes/collects then sums rows. README pins baseline commit `3a72f8a61e14613f517dded6816d4bfc77817c93`, lists six SHA-256 values and requires using baseline writers for independent evidence.
